data.narrative:
MatX is a Series B semiconductor company founded by Reiner Pope and Mike Gunter that has raised $500M+. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 8 private and 3 public comparables in the chips and semiconductors sector, including same-stage and adjacent-stage private companies (Positron AI, SambaNova Systems, d-Matrix, DEEPX) and public references (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the $500M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, yielding $950M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector comparables spanning Series A through Series C stages produces a median valuation of $1.5B, with a range of $529M to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied because MatX's revenue is not on file. The wide peer range reflects stage and scale dispersion within the semiconductor frontier-tech cohort.

Triangulating the two applicable methods produces a valuation range of $808M to $1.7B, with a median of $1.2B. Key uncertainties include MatX's revenue profile relative to peers (necessary for P/S anchoring) and the appropriate stage-progression multiple given actual funding velocity and burn characteristics. The spread between stage-progression ($950M) and peer-median ($1.5B) reflects tension between raised capital and peer valuations in an early-stage, capital-intensive sector.
